composers_checked.name: Krommer, Franz
composers_checked.note: All 146 IMSLP pages accounted for; floor from commercial recordings only (no concert documentation sought). Gap check done against the Wikipedia/Padrta list and Earsense.

note: Krommer (c43): 45 works kept (32 from 28 IMSLP pages, 13 found by the gap check); 118 pages skipped, 32 of them as duplicates. Floor evidence is Apple Music track lists (iTunes API: 79 albums with Krommer in the metadata, chamber albums looked up), MusicBrainz releases (Claves, Regis, ARS), Earsense's per-work recording credits and reviews at classical-music.com and MusicWeb. AllMusic, Presto and the Naxos Music Library could not be read (403/login), so catalogue numbers are given only where a source showed them; Hungaroton, Tudor and most Supraphon numbers are missing. Anthology discs that name Krommer only in a track title could be missed. Not found on any source: a recording of any string quintet, of the piano trios Op. 84/87 or of the other string quartets; all are skipped. Conflicts: (1) Op. 53 No. 1 is C minor on the Tudor disc but E-flat in Padrta's list, Wikipedia and Earsense, so its title has no key. (2) Op. 21: IMSLP, CPO and the Tudor disc call the E-flat quartet No. 1, Padrta and Supraphon call it No. 2; the other numbering is in aka. (3) Op. 5 No. 1: IMSLP dates it c. 1810, Earsense 1796 (Krommer's early opus numbers date from the 1790s); c. 1796 used. (4) The oboe quintets are oboe, violin, two violas, cello (Regis review and the Naxos personnel); Earsense says two violins. (5) Flute quintets: Earsense lists the nine quintets (Opp. 49, 55, 58, 63, 66, 92, 101, 104, 109) with one Bruno Meier/Stamitz Quartet recording each, and a search snippet of Meier's Naxos Music Library biography (page itself unreadable, 403) says he recorded all nine with the Stamitz Quartet; only Koch Schwann 3-1049-2 (three quintets, review at classical-music.com) was confirmed as a disc, so confidence is medium. (6) The Padrta (P.) numbers in aka come from IMSLP and the Wikipedia work list; Krommer's opus numbers repeat (Op. 92 and 95 are used twice), so titles are by opus, key and scoring. Tudor's 'Partita, Op. 69' is the E-flat Clarinet Quartet. Gap check against the Wikipedia/Padrta list: added the string quartets Op. 7, the bassoon quartets Op. 46, Op. 47, Op. 82, the posthumous clarinet quartet, flute quintets Opp. 49 and 63 and the oboe quartet/quintets. Other Padrta works in scope (string quartets Opp. 4 and 10, string quintets Opp. 18, 62 and 102, flute quintet Op. 25, flute quartets Opp. 23 and 94, the Rosinack oboe quintets) have no IMSLP page and no recording found, so were not added.
